mode_evidence: The sign is first apprehended by constantly looking with the eye, then the counterpart sign appears 'free from the kasina disk', in space ('like a crystal fan in space'), a purified, more definitely visualised image; the translator's note says the counterpart sign is 'more definitely visualized image' than the Pitaka usage. The digest does not itself say the image lies in the visual field with eyes shut (the search agent's hint to that effect was not visible).
onset_evidence: A full induction: prepare the kasina object, sit, look at it with eyes moderately open, repeat the name ('light, light'), and the learning sign then counterpart sign arise. Those with previous-life practice get the sign on seeing the object in nature; others must prepare one. A blunt statement of difficulty: the preliminary work is difficult for a beginner and only one in a hundred or a thousand can do it, and arousing the sign is again that hard. No fixed time scale in the digest.

conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: Eyes open moderately, as if seeing one's face reflected in a mirror; not reviewing the colour or characteristic.
conditions.setting: Screened place on the outskirts of the monastery; for light kasina, a circle of sun or moonlight through a hole in a wall or a lamp in a pot with a hole facing a wall.
conditions.prerequisites: Previous-life practice makes the sign arise easily in nature; beings hindered by kamma, defilement or lack of faith cannot develop any kasina.

stages.label: learning sign (uggaha-nimitta)
stages.description: Like the object, with its faults (embers, smoke, stamens); for the light kasina like the circle thrown on wall or ground.

stages.label: counterpart sign (patibhaga-nimitta)
stages.description: Purified, motionless, free of the disk: crystal fan in space, red cloth or gold fan for fire, compact bright cluster of lights for light.

stages.label: extended light for divine eye
stages.description: Light kasina extended at access level; repeated entry into basic jhana consolidates light in the delimited area.

what_to_do_with_light: Apprehend and develop the sign; protect and extend it; for the divine eye extend the light kasina at access level and renew it by repeatedly entering jhana and pervading with light, until it stays in the area delimited ('Let there be light here').
obstacles_and_fixes: Eyes too wide: fatigue and the disk too obvious; too narrow: drowsiness and the disk not obvious. Keep them moderately open.
Light disappears when the preliminary work's turn runs out: re-enter basic jhana, emerge and pervade with light again.
cautions: Do not review the colour or attend to its characteristic.
Kasina work is very difficult; only one in a hundred or a thousand succeeds at the preliminary work.
interpretation: The signs are mind-made abstractions of the kasina object, the counterpart sign being the basis for access and absorption jhana; the light kasina grounds the divine eye and the torch simile shows the light as a temporary aid.
practice_summary: Choose your kasina: for light, take the circle thrown on a wall or floor by sun or moon through a hole, or put a lamp in a pot with a hole facing a wall. Sit comfortably and look with eyes open moderately, as if seeing your reflection in a mirror, neither strained nor drowsy. Do not review the colour or characteristic. Repeat 'light, light' and keep apprehending the sign. The learning sign comes, like the circle; then the counterpart sign appears, a compact bright cluster of lights, which leads to access and absorption. To extend it for the divine eye, keep it at access level, then enter basic jhana again and again and pervade the area with light, until it holds.

key_passages.locator: Ch. IV earth kasina section 28, source lines 11062-11098
key_passages.anchor: keeping his eyes open moderately, as if he were seeing the reflection of his face
key_passages.paraphrase: Eyes open moderately, like looking at one's reflection in a mirror.

key_passages.anchor: If he opens his eyes too wide, they get fatigued and the disk becomes too obvious, which prevents the sign becoming apparent to him.
key_passages.paraphrase: Eye opening is a troubleshooting variable: too wide or too narrow both prevent the sign.

key_passages.locator: Ch. V light kasina sections 21-23, source lines 13832-13910
key_passages.anchor: The counterpart sign is like a compact bright cluster of lights.
key_passages.paraphrase: The light kasina is the circle of sun, moon or lamp light on a wall; its counterpart sign looks like a compact bright cluster of lights.

key_passages.anchor: is difficult for a beginner and only one in a hundred or a thousand can do it.
key_passages.paraphrase: The author states that kasina preliminary work, and arousing the sign afterwards, succeed for only about one in a hundred or a thousand.

key_passages.anchor: Then he should again and again attain the basic jhana, emerge and pervade with light.
key_passages.paraphrase: When the extended light fades, re-enter jhana and pervade with light until it consolidates in the delimited area.
